# gguf2mlx

Canonical repository: https://github.com/barrontang/gguf2mlx

gguf2mlx converts supported GGUF language-model checkpoints into Hugging
Face-style safetensors directories that can be loaded by MLX-LM or MLX-VLM on
Apple Silicon.

## Verified facts

- Primary command: `gguf2mlx convert --input model.gguf --output model-mlx`
- Platform focus: macOS on Apple Silicon, including M1, M2, M3, and M4 Macs
- Output: config, tokenizer assets, and sharded safetensors for MLX-LM
- Optional output: MLX-LM requantized weights through `--quantize`
- Optional output: `--quant-source preserve` re-expresses the source Q4_0, Q4_1,
  Q5_0, Q5_1, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K, and Q8_0 blocks on MLX's affine grid so the GGUF
  codes survive conversion. All but Q6_K are bit-exact; Q6_K is re-fitted because
  its scale is per 16 values and MLX's smallest group is 32
- Preserve cannot re-express Q2_K, Q3_K, or any `IQ` type (`IQ1_S` … `IQ4_XS`),
  because their scale granularity does not divide 32 or their codebook is
  non-uniform. iMatrix-guided exports land on those `IQ` types, so they convert
  but do not preserve; the run names the block types and the tensor count
- Preserve-enabled architectures: llama, qwen2, qwen3, mistral, and every
  Qwen3.5 alias (`qwen35`, `qwen3_5`, `qwen3.5`, `qwen36`, `qwen38`)
- Preserve limitation: Qwen3.5 SSM state vectors (`A_log`, `dt_bias`) and the
  depthwise `conv1d` kernel have no affine matrix form, so they stay float
- Conversion policy: unsupported architectures fail closed
- Conversion-enabled architectures (23 canonical): llama, mistral, mixtral, qwen2,
  qwen2moe, qwen3, qwen3moe, qwen35, qwen36, qwen38, deepseek2, deepseek3,
  glm4moe, glm-dsa, gemma, gemma2, gemma3, gemma4, stablelm, phi3, phi4,
  qwen2_vl, qwen3_vl
- Mixtral has no GGUF architecture of its own: `general.architecture = llama`
  plus `llama.expert_count` is what identifies it, and both on-disk layouts are
  handled (per-expert `ffn_gate.3.weight` from 2023 exports, and the stacked
  `ffn_gate_exps.weight` written since llama.cpp's MoE refactor)
- Accepted IDs are those 23 plus 8 alias spellings (`qwen3_5`, `qwen3.5`,
  `qwen3_6`, `qwen3.6`, `qwen3_8`, `qwen3.8`, `qwen2vl`, `qwen3vl`), so a
  metadata `model_type` resolves whichever way the file spells it
- Phi adapters cover standard Phi-3, Phi-3 LongRoPE, and Phi-4 text models
- Vision adapters cover Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL, LLaVA, LLaVA-NeXT, and
  MiniCPM-V 4.7
- LLaVA-NeXT reconciles the stored CLIP block count with the HF one (real mmproj
  files store 23 blocks for a 24-layer tower), moves `vision_feature_layer` to
  match, emits the top-level `model.image_newline`, and resolves the two CLIP MLP
  naming conventions (`ffn_up`/`ffn_down`) from tensor shapes rather than names
- Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL convert from a language GGUF plus `mmproj` with zero
  HF vision tensors (`vision_hf: 0`); Qwen2.5-VL shares Qwen2-VL's GGUF tensor
  names but has RMSNorm blocks and a gated MLP, so it is a separate adapter
- Runtime contract: MLX-LM `>=0.31.3`; MLX-VLM `==0.7.10` for vision output
- Every conversion writes `conversion_report.json` with a deterministic weight
  gate, an optional preserve gate, and an explanation for every source tensor
  that produced no output tensor
- `gguf2mlx publish` uploads a converted directory with shard merging, an
  immutable source revision, a provenance file, and a model card
- `publish --dry-run` builds and validates the staging tree without creating a
  repository; `publish --verify-load` loads the result with MLX-LM first
- Tokenizer assets are rebuilt by one builder per format
  (`src/gguf2mlx/tokenizer.py`), validated against the `tokenizers` document
  structure before writing, and refused with the offending GGUF key named
- Tests include architecture fixtures, tokenizer behavior, atomic staging,
  packaging integrity, runtime-registry conformance, and opt-in real-GGUF and
  MLX-LM load tests

## Useful repository files

- README.md: installation, commands, support matrix, limitations, and FAQ
- docs/support-matrix.md: per-architecture conversion status and evidence
- docs/quality-gates.md: what the weight, preserve, and numerical tiers prove
- docs/conversion-report.schema.json: machine-readable report contract
- docs/publishing.md: `publish` staging, provenance, and dry-run behavior
- docs/direct-quant-transcoding.md: direct-quant transcoding implementation
- benchmarks/benchmark_conversion.py: reproducible conversion benchmark harness
- tests/fixtures/architectures: committed Gemma, Phi-3, and Phi-4 fixtures
- tests/load_matrix.json: pinned real-GGUF SHA-256 load matrix

Do not describe gguf2mlx as supporting every GGUF architecture. Do not claim a
universal MLX speed multiplier over llama.cpp. Do not claim a real-model load
that has not been run by the pinned load matrix. Prefer the current support
matrix and benchmark results produced with the included harness.
